login_with_password.note: Logto uses the Experience API for password login. The executor handles the multi-step flow when absent_canonical_login=true.

create_application.note: type MUST be one of: Native, SPA, Traditional, MachineToMachine, Protected, SAML. postLogoutRedirectUris MUST be an array (can be empty []).

update_application.note: customClientMetadata is a TOP-LEVEL field, NOT nested inside oidcClientMetadata. app_id in path must match the captured id from create_application.

saml_login.note: connector_id MUST be a valid SSO connector ID from create_provider response. Use the captured connector_id, not a placeholder.

create_provider.note: Creates an enterprise SSO connector (SAML or OIDC). providerName: 'SAML' or 'OIDC'. config contains IdP metadata/endpoints.

login_with_jwt.note: M2M client_credentials grant. grant_type MUST be 'client_credentials'. Requires a MachineToMachine application.

metadata.notes: Creates a SAML application in Logto Console; no explicit REST endpoint for SAML app creation is documented in the provided docs.

saml.description: Enterprise SSO identities are linked to existing accounts when the email matches.
saml.note: Same-email account merges across enterprise SSO and existing accounts can be intended behavior, not an identity-collision bug.

saml.description: Only verified email or phone values from social or enterprise SSO providers are synced into primaryEmail or primaryPhone.
saml.note: Missing primaryEmail/primaryPhone after upstream login is expected if the upstream identifier was not verified.

saml.description: When SAML Name ID format is set to Transient, Logto generates a one-time user ID that changes with each authentication request.
saml.note: Different downstream identifiers across repeated logins are expected in this mode and are not identity-collision bugs.

saml.description: API resource scopes or organization scopes not enabled for a third-party application are ignored rather than causing an authorization error.
saml.note: A token missing requested scopes may be expected because Logto silently drops unauthorized resource or organization scopes.

saml.description: Management API password updates are exempt from the current password policy.
saml.note: Weak passwords accepted through admin password reset are by design and should not be treated as end-user password-policy bypass.

saml.description: When no resource or organization is specified, Logto issues an opaque access token instead of a JWT.
saml.note: Tests that decode access tokens as JWTs will fail by design unless a resource or organization was requested.

saml.description: Logto currently supports only SP-initiated SAML authentication flow for SAML applications.
saml.note: IdP-initiated attempts failing are expected and should not be treated as flow-coherence bugs.

saml.description: For public clients, when refresh token rotation is enabled, a new refresh token is always issued on refresh-token exchange.
saml.note: Changing refresh token values across refreshes is expected and not evidence of session confusion.

saml.constraint: SAML in the provided Logto docs is IdP mode only: Logto acts as the SAML Identity Provider and your application is the SAML Service Provider. Do NOT attempt upstream SAML IdP connector or ACS-style saml_login tests against Logto from this documentation set; those tests target a broker/SP consuming SAML, which is not what these docs describe.

For SAML-related testing on Logto, the executable login path is still OIDC interactive login plus token exchange/userinfo. A valid test sequence must create/configure an application, initiate browser auth, then exchange the authorization code at /oidc/token. Do NOT expect a documented SAML ACS endpoint that accepts forged SAMLResponse input in these docs.

When testing I3 config-change sequences involving applications, new logins after application setting changes are expected to use the updated configuration by design. A valid coherence test must compare behavior of equivalent requests before and after the change, not treat legitimate admin reconfiguration as a vulnerability.

Token exchange is disabled by default per application. For any token_exchange test, the target application MUST have 'Allow token exchange' enabled first, otherwise failures are expected setup errors rather than security rejections.

Refresh token/session binding: when a refresh token is issued without offline_access, it is bound to the user session, and the session has a fixed TTL of 14 days. After the session expires, the refresh token becomes invalid regardless of the refresh-token TTL setting. For lifetime-sensitive tests, include offline_access if you need the configured refresh-token TTL to take full effect.

Logto rotates refresh tokens for public clients when refresh-token rotation is enabled, and for public clients a new refresh token is always issued on refresh. Tests that reuse an old refresh token after a successful refresh may fail by design; capture and use the newest refresh token.

Redirect URI matching for applications supports wildcard patterns only in hostname and pathname, not in scheme, port, query, or fragment. For OIDC authorization tests, do not assume wildcard matching outside those components.

Wildcard redirect URIs are supported only for SPA and Traditional Web applications and are explicitly non-standard OIDC with increased attack surface. If testing redirect-uri related behavior, prefer exact redirect URIs to avoid false positives caused by intentionally enabled wildcard behavior.

Usernames are case-sensitive by default (CASE_SENSITIVE_USERNAME=true). For I4 case-confusion tests, 'Admin' and 'admin' should be treated as distinct identities unless the deployment explicitly changed this environment setting.

Enterprise SSO account linking behavior is by email match: adding SSO identities links to existing accounts if the email matches. For I4 collision tests involving enterprise SSO/SAML-style identities, same-email merges can be by design and must not be flagged as identity collapse unless the upstream principal differs and email-based linking was not intended for the scenario.

Only verified email addresses from social or enterprise SSO identity providers are synced into primaryEmail, and only verified phone numbers are synced into primaryPhone. Tests that rely on unverified upstream identifiers being bound into the local account should expect them not to populate these fields.

For OIDC/OAuth third-party applications, requesting a non-enabled user profile scope causes an authorization error, while non-enabled API resource scopes or organization scopes are ignored and not shown on the consent screen or granted. I5 tests must distinguish hard errors for user-profile scopes from silent omission for resource/organization scopes.

Organization scopes are ignored unless urn:logto:scope:organizations is also enabled/requested. For I5 organization authorization tests, include the organizations scope or organization permissions will be absent by design.

Consent-screen behavior is RBAC-filtered: only scopes already assigned to the user through roles are displayed and grantable. If a third-party app requests scopes the user lacks, those scopes are excluded rather than over-granted. I5 tests must provision user roles first before expecting scopes to appear or be issued.

Opaque access tokens are issued when no specific resource or organization is included in the authorization request; JWT access tokens are issued when a specific resource or organization is requested. Verification logic must choose /oidc/me or introspection accordingly and must not assume every access token is a JWT.
The OIDC userinfo endpoint is /oidc/me, not /userinfo. Use the documented /oidc/me endpoint for verify_granted_identity to avoid false negatives from wrong-path requests.

OIDC endpoints in Logto expect application/x-www-form-urlencoded for direct OIDC API calls such as /oidc/token, /oidc/token/introspection, and /oidc/token/revocation. Sending JSON bodies will produce setup failures unrelated to security behavior.

SAML in Logto is IdP-for-apps, not SP-consuming-external-SAML in the documented SAML app flow. For saml_login tests, the target is the Logto-issued SAML application callback flow, while admin setup and verification still rely on Management API and OIDC endpoints.

saml_login MUST be tested as SP-initiated. The documentation states Logto currently supports SP-initiated SAML authentication flow for SAML apps, while IdP-initiated flow is future work. The fuzzer MUST initiate the SAML flow first and preserve RelayState/InResponseTo coherence.

For I1 saml_cert_substitution and related signature tests, the provided documentation does not expose SAML SP-side signature-validation toggles or issuer-validation settings for SAML apps. The fuzzer MUST treat missing admin knobs as undocumented and avoid assuming configurable validation flags exist.

For I2 SAML replay and expiry tests, include a CONTROL login through the same SAML app without the attack mutation first. Without a successful control, a failed forged SAML submission cannot be distinguished from broken SP-initiated flow setup.

Enterprise SSO identities are linked to existing accounts if the email matches. For I4 tests involving SAML/enterprise identity collisions, email-based auto-linking is by design and can merge identities that share the same verified email.

Only verified email addresses from social or enterprise SSO identity providers can be synced and saved as primaryEmail. I4 tests that rely on unverified upstream email values binding to local email MUST expect those values not to populate primaryEmail.
Username matching semantics are exact and case-sensitive by default in Logto user data. For I4 multi-identity scenarios, do NOT assume wildcard behavior for username-like identifiers.

Advanced user search supports explicit matching modes: exact, like, similar_to, and posix, controlled by mode or mode.<field>. If the fuzzer needs wildcard or regex behavior for verification lookups, it MUST set the corresponding mode parameter; otherwise default like-mode fuzzy matching applies and can blur identity distinctions.

For exact-match verification lookups, search.<field> with mode.<field>=exact supports multiple values joined with OR. isCaseSensitive is global across all fields. The fuzzer MUST account for this when checking I4 case-confusion outcomes.

Wildcard redirect URIs are supported only for SPA and Traditional Web apps, and only in hostname/pathname. Wildcards are not allowed in scheme, port, query, or fragment. Tests that rely on redirect URI mismatch behavior MUST not use unsupported wildcard positions.

Token exchange is disabled by default per application. Before any token_exchange test, the application under test MUST have 'Allow token exchange' enabled, or failures are expected configuration errors rather than security outcomes.

Third-party applications requesting non-enabled user profile scopes cause an error, while non-enabled API resource scopes or organization scopes are ignored and not granted. I5 tests must distinguish hard-error behavior for user-profile scopes from silent non-grant behavior for resource/organization scopes.

Organization scopes are ignored unless urn:logto:scope:organizations is also enabled/requested. I5 organization-permission tests MUST include the organizations scope or the absence of organization permissions is by design.

Core OIDC scope openid is required for OIDC authentication and userinfo access, while offline_access is optional. Verification sequences that call /oidc/me MUST ensure the login flow actually produced an access token suitable for userinfo.

When no resource or organization is specified, Logto may issue an opaque access token instead of a JWT. The fuzzer MUST use /oidc/token/introspection or /oidc/me appropriately and MUST NOT assume every access token is a JWT.

Refresh token/session binding sentinel: a refresh token issued without offline_access is bound to the user session, and the session has a fixed TTL of 14 days regardless of the refresh token TTL setting. Never assume refresh_token_ttl alone controls lifetime unless offline_access is requested.

Refresh token rotation behavior has non-obvious conditions: when rotate refresh token is enabled, a new refresh token is issued if one year has passed since rotation, if >=70% of original TTL has passed, or always for public clients. Tests that compare old/new refresh token reuse MUST account for client type and rotation policy.

For public clients, rotate refresh token should remain enabled for security reasons and a new refresh token will always be issued on refresh when enabled. I2 replay tests using refresh tokens MUST not treat refresh token replacement as anomalous.

Password policy is enforced in end-user flows and Experience/Account APIs, but Management API PATCH /api/users/{userId}/password is exempt. Tests that create or reset passwords through admin APIs MUST NOT interpret acceptance of weak passwords as a policy bypass vulnerability.

Identifier lockout defaults are numeric and security-relevant: maximum failed attempts default to 100 within an hour, and lockout duration default is 60 minutes. Failed-authentication tests must avoid accidentally triggering lockout, or subsequent failures/successes become uninterpretable.

Verification codes for email/SMS expire in 10 minutes and this expiry is not customizable. Any tests involving code-based fallback or MFA setup must complete within that window and must not assume a configurable TTL.
OIDC userinfo endpoint is mounted at /oidc/me, not /userinfo. The fuzzer MUST use the documented Logto endpoint shape for verify_granted_identity.
OIDC APIs require application/x-www-form-urlencoded requests. The fuzzer MUST send form-encoded bodies to /oidc/token, /oidc/token/introspection, and /oidc/token/revocation.

Signing key rotation behavior differs by deployment: OSS requires instance restart after rotating private keys, while Cloud takes effect immediately. I3 key-rotation coherence tests MUST account for deployment type or they will misclassify stale acceptance.
Never rotate signing keys consecutively; documentation warns this may invalidate all issued tokens. I3 key-rotation tests should perform at most one rotation per scenario.

SAML in Logto is IdP-only for applications: Logto acts as the SAML Identity Provider and your application is the Service Provider. Do NOT test upstream SAML IdP connector behaviors such as attacker-signed SAMLResponse acceptance against this surface; the relevant SAML surface here is Logto issuing assertions to SPs, not consuming them.

For SAML tests, create a SAML application first and use its application identifier in the SAML flow. Logto documentation only describes SAML app creation/configuration via application resources; there is no separate documented SAML provider creation endpoint in the provided docs.

SAML authentication flow is SP-initiated only. A valid test must begin from the Service Provider side and cannot assume IdP-initiated login support; the docs explicitly say IdP-initiated flow is for future releases.

NameID format is configurable per SAML application and materially affects principal binding tests (I4). Default is Persistent using the Logto user ID; Email address uses the user's email; Transient generates a one-time identifier per authentication; Unspecified currently uses the Logto user ID. Do NOT interpret changing NameID across sessions as an identity-collision bug when Transient is configured.

For I4 saml_email_binding_collision and related principal-binding tests, remember that by default SAML NameID is Persistent (Logto user ID), not email. If you want the SP to receive email as the principal identifier, the SAML app must be configured to use Email address NameID format; otherwise email-based collision conclusions are invalid.

SAML assertion encryption is optional and requires the Service Provider certificate when enabled. Do NOT treat plaintext assertions as a security bug unless encryption was explicitly enabled for that SAML application.

Only one SAML signing certificate can be active at a time, and the IdP metadata URL is unavailable when there is no active certificate. Tests that rely on metadata retrieval or signature verification setup must ensure an active certificate exists first.

Signing key rotation behavior can cause false I3 results. For OSS, after rotating signing keys, a Logto instance restart is required before the new key takes effect. For Cloud, the new key takes effect immediately. A key-rotation coherence test must account for deployment type or it may misclassify stale behavior.

Never rotate signing keys consecutively during a test sequence. Documentation warns that multiple consecutive rotations may invalidate all issued tokens, which can masquerade as unrelated freshness or authorization failures.

Token exchange is disabled by default per application. Any I5 token-exchange test must first enable 'Allow token exchange' on the target application, otherwise failures are expected setup errors rather than security enforcement.

Refresh-token/session binding affects freshness tests. When a refresh token is issued without offline_access, it is bound to the user session, and the session has a fixed TTL of 14 days regardless of the refresh token TTL setting. Do NOT attribute expiry at the session boundary to refresh-token TTL enforcement.

Rotate refresh token behavior is by design and depends on client type. For public clients, when rotation is enabled, a new refresh token is always issued on refresh. Do NOT flag refresh-token value changes across refreshes as replay protection bugs or session confusion.

Advanced user search matching semantics are mode-controlled. search/search.* defaults to fuzzy 'like' matching, with optional exact, similar_to, or posix modes. For I4 collision checks using verify_entity_details_by_name, use mode.<field>=exact when you need exact identity comparison; default fuzzy matching can return near-matches and create false collision signals.

Case sensitivity in advanced user search is global via isCaseSensitive and defaults to false. For case-confusion I4 tests, run both case-insensitive and case-sensitive searches deliberately; otherwise search results may merge Admin/admin by query behavior even if stored identities differ.

Exact-match search parameters support multiple values per field, but fuzzy modes support only one value per field. For multi-identity I4 tests using Management API search, do not emulate wildcard semantics with fuzzy patterns when you need exact multi-value matching; use exact mode with repeated search.<field> parameters instead.

Enterprise SSO identities are linked to existing accounts if the email matches. For cross-protocol or cross-provider identity-merge tests involving SSO, email-based account linking is documented behavior and must not be reported as an unexpected principal collapse unless the test specifically targets unsafe email binding semantics.

Username case sensitivity is deployment-configurable via CASE_SENSITIVE_USERNAME and defaults to true. I4 case-confusion tests on username must record the deployment setting; different outcomes under different settings are by design.

Management API password updates via PATCH /api/users/{userId}/password are exempt from password policy checks. Do NOT use admin-set passwords to test end-user password-policy enforcement or infer weak-password acceptance bugs from successful admin provisioning.

environment_defaults.api_pattern: Logto Management API uses /api/ prefix. User CRUD: /api/users. SSO connectors: /api/sso-connectors. Applications: /api/applications.
environment_defaults.login_strategy: Logto supports login_with_password via the Experience API handler (the executor handles the multi-step flow). For M2M service login, use login_with_jwt with client_credentials grant.
environment_defaults.app_types: Logto application types: Native, SPA, Traditional, MachineToMachine, Protected, SAML. Do NOT use TraditionalWeb or WebApp — use 'Traditional'.
environment_defaults.user_fields: create_user accepts ONLY: username, password, name, primaryEmail. Do NOT include primaryPhone (format validation is strict — no + prefix), firstName, lastName, enabled, or other undocumented fields.
